vendor_review_notes.assessment: Debian confirms installed SQLite source version 3.40.1-2+deb12u2 vulnerable; bookworm no-dsa minor-issue policy is not a fix or accepted exception. Trivy imports NVD CRITICAL severity.

Vendor description limits the overflow to 32-bit Perl builds. Archive observation identifies /usr/bin/perl as ELF64 x86-64; this is an applicability discrepancy for owner review, not a suppressed finding or accepted exception.

Upstream identifies setuptools PackageIndex download code and fix 78.1.1. Runtime pip vendor.txt records setuptools 70.3.0, but no setuptools/package_index.py path was observed in archive layers. Trivy used embedded SBOM package identity; exact vendored subset/reachability needs review before disposition.

Upstream describes source-distribution building and Unicode normalization, especially macOS APFS/HFS+. Selected artifact is a Linux installed-wheel runtime; this scope distinction needs owner review and does not authorize an exception. Trivy records fixed version 83.0.0.

limitations: No exploitability proof or waiver is inferred from scanner counts, vendor status, absent current finding, or advisory severity.
All 107 native package/version/architecture inventory rows match the prior image, so native finding changes cannot be attributed to package remediation.
Current binary-package occurrences and old Scout source-package advisories have different counting units; compare normalized source/package IDs with explicit alias handling.
Trivy warns that embedded third-party SBOM metadata may cause inaccurate detection; archive vendor.txt confirms recorded msgpack 1.1.2 and setuptools 70.3.0.
No secrets or misconfiguration scanning, attack simulation, production endpoint testing, release qualification or accepted security exception was performed.

Several requested Debian vendor page reads returned web-tool Failed to fetch restricted URL; those reads were stopped without retry. Raw advisory references remain retained; independent vendor review is incomplete for those pages.
